judgments.reasoning_cat1: Pure cross-reference.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 16.7 does define Voidable Transfer as cross-referenced.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Names a single institution; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Base Rate definition, the Bank Product Provider definition and Section 2.6(a)'s sole-bank requirement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The deeming rule is qualified by "unless the context clearly requires otherwise", which reintroduces the very uncertainty it is meant to remove.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 7.16 is drafted around "Fund's Tangible Net Worth" while the Senior Leverage Ratio definition speaks of "Obligations of Borrower" — the deeming rule has to do real work to reconcile them, and it does so only imperfectly.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A clear priority rule with an Article 9 tie-break; well constructed.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Code definition and Section 13(a)'s New York governing law.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It fixes several potentially contested usages ("including" is not limiting, "or" means and/or), but the deeming of any Record as satisfying a writing requirement and as a warranty of accuracy is a strong rule buried at the end.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The "repayment in full" gloss must be read with Sections 3.6, 3.7 and 2.3(b)(iii)'s own "paid in full" definition, which are not identical formulations.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sentence incorporation clause; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The table of contents numbers this provision 1.4 while the body numbers it 1.5, and several referenced schedules and Exhibit L-1 are not attached to the executed document.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A simple lesser-of formula; the commitment language is definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The $50,000,000 Maximum Revolver Amount and a 20% Borrowing Base cannot both be used while complying with Section 7.16(b)'s 0.9% Senior Leverage Ratio cap against a $600,000,000 Tangible Net Worth floor.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: An unbounded reserve right ("in such amounts, and with respect to such matters, as Lender ... shall deem necessary or appropriate, ... including" four illustrative categories) is followed by a sentence withdrawing it absent a Triggering Event — the general grant and the specific limit sit uneasily, and clauses (iii) and (iv) overlap.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The limiting sentence requires a Triggering Event that "has occurred and is continuing", but the Triggering Event definition itself omits the continuation requirement; the Borrowing Base definition also deducts these reserves without repeating the limit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The second limit is bizarre as written: unused availability plus cash in the Cash Management Accounts may not exceed Fund's unfunded commitments to makers, which would extinguish availability whenever unfunded commitments are small.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It cannot easily be harmonised with Section 2.1(a)'s commitment to lend up to the lesser of the cap and the Borrowing Base, or with Section 7.14's permitted use of proceeds for working capital and general corporate needs.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A one-sentence revolving-credit statement; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 2.1(a), 3.4 and 3.7.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[I]ncluding without limitation the conditions set forth in Section 3.3" leaves the universe of conditions open-ended.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Sections 3.1 and 3.3 set out the conditions; the open reference is broader than either but not inconsistent with them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "At Lender's election, in lieu of delivering the above-described written request, any Authorized Person may give Lender telephonic notice" is confused about whose election it is, and the same-day noon deadline is unusually tight.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.8 lets Lender act on instructions from "anyone purporting to be an Authorized Person" and even without instructions under Section 2.5(c), which is broader than the procedure prescribed here.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Mechanical funding provision, conditioned on satisfaction of terms; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Designated Account definition, Section 2.8 and Section 6.18's Settlement Agent funding requirement.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise cut-off with a deemed-receipt rule; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.7 states the same cut-off but deems late items received at the opening of the next Business Day, while this clause deems them received on the following Business Day with interest continuing to accrue; the two overlap without contradicting.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A carefully ordered eight-tier waterfall with an express definition of "paid in full"; long but determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Clause (iv) itself anticipates conflicts with other Loan Documents and gives this Section priority, which is a drafted answer rather than an unresolved inconsistency.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It measures an Overadvance by "the amount of Obligations ... owed pursuant to Section 2.1", a mismatch with Section 2.1's limits which are expressed in terms of Advances and Revolver Usage.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.1(c) states the limits in terms of Revolver Usage and Section 2.3(b)(D) refers to Overadvances being "created"; the definitional mismatch runs across these provisions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A two-branch rate provision keyed to defined terms; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 2.12 and 2.5(b) and the Applicable Margin definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The default rate is set at four points above the rate applicable to Base Rate Loans but is applied to "all Obligations", so LIBOR loans are repriced off a different index — a workable but non-obvious result.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.12(a) separately lets Lender convert LIBOR loans to Base Rate on an Event of Default, so two mechanisms address the same situation.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The self-charging and interest-compounding mechanics are spelled out in detail; the phrase "at any time that Lender has an obligation to extend credit" as a payment trigger is slightly odd.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It defers expressly to Section 2.10 and is qualified by Section 2.5(e)'s usury savings; consistent.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A 360-day/actual-days convention plus automatic Base Rate adjustment; standard and definite.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the Base Rate definition and Section 2.5(e)'s cap.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional usury savings clause; its "ipso facto ... as of the date of this Agreement" formulation is dense but its effect is stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.10(e) repeats a nonusurious-amount proviso, consistent with this clause.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The clause is a dense multi-limb covenant, but the sting is the final sentence making Wells Fargo "the only Cash Management Bank" after 60 days.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.6(c) expressly permits Administrative Borrower to add or replace Cash Management Banks and Accounts thereafter, which the final sentence of this clause forecloses — a direct tension between two subsections of the same Section.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Prescribes three required terms with "among other things", leaving the balance to Lender's satisfaction.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.6(e) requires a differently specified Cash Management Agreement for Escrow Accounts (agent/bailee-in-possession, no daily sweep), so the required terms are not uniform.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Two closure deadlines (30 days for creditworthiness, 60 days for performance) triggered by Lender's "reasonable judgment"; the standards are stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It grants an amendment right that the last sentence of Section 2.6(a) appears to remove after 60 days from the Closing Date; the two cannot both be given full effect.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short, definite grant and characterisation.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 4.1's grant and Section 4.7's control requirement, though the Cash Management Accounts are held in "Fund's name" only under 2.6(a)(ii) while each Borrower purports to grant a Lien in them.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The carve-out "except accounts belonging to an Account Debtor of Borrower" is undefined in scope, and the clause shifts mid-sentence from "Escrow Account" to "Cash Management Account".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 6.17 requires deposit of *all* escrowed amounts, expressly including funds held on behalf of any Account Debtor, into a Deposit Account subject to Lender's Lien — the opposite of this carve-out.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Precise rules on when payment items count and when they are deemed received.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.3(a) states a parallel but not identical deemed-receipt rule; a small redundancy rather than a conflict.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[A]nyone purporting to be an Authorized Person" is a strikingly broad authorisation, and the sentence contains a duplicated "establish establish".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.2(a) prescribes a written request by an Authorized Person, so this clause materially relaxes the borrowing procedure set out there.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The "absent manifest error ... conclusively presumed to be correct" account-stated mechanism with a 30-day objection window is a common site of argument but is precisely stated.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 2.5(c) and 2.7's crediting rules.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A single figure earned on a stated date; nothing to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the chapeau's non-refundability rule and Section 3.7's separate prepayment premium.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The sentence omits the noun — "a monthly loan administration equal to $2,000" — a drafting slip, though the intended meaning (a fee) is obvious.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 2.5(c)'s authority to charge fees to the Loan Account.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The rate is written "one-half of one percent (0.30%)" — the words and the numeral state different figures — and the "greater of (A) ... or (y) $20,000,000" formula is mis-lettered and hard to apply.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Applicable Margin definition writes the same words as "(0.50%)", showing which figure was intended, and Section 2.10(e) imposes a separate minimum-interest charge on the same $20,000,000 baseline, raising a double-charging question.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A fixed per-diem fee plus "actual reasonable and customary charges" for third parties; the latter is open but qualified.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The Lender Expenses definition caps appraisal and audit charges "up to the amount of any limitation contained in this Agreement", and this clause is the only such limitation; they fit.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A dense hypothetical-interest computation, but every input is specified and a usury proviso is attached.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It overlaps with the Section 2.10(c) unused line fee, which uses the same $20,000,000 floor during the Minimum Interest Period, so a borrower could argue it is charged twice for the same shortfall.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A conventional capital-adequacy yield protection clause; the payment period is garbled ("$0 days") and the amount is one "deemed by Lender to be material".
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 16.5's gross-up regime; no conflict identified.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It states a default rule that LIBOR loans convert to Base Rate at each Interest Period end unless the option has been exercised.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.12(c) reverses that default by deeming a LIBOR election for every Interest Period unless Borrower opts out — the two subsections state opposite defaults.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A precise notice deadline with a confirmation mechanic; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It presupposes an affirmative election, whereas Section 2.12(c) makes the election automatic; and it refers to "a permitted portion of the Advances" although Section 2.12(a) speaks of "all of the Advances".

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Clear on its own terms as a deemed-election rule with an opt-out.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It contradicts Section 2.12(a)'s automatic conversion to Base Rate absent an exercised option, and shifts from "Administrative Borrower" to "Borrower" as the actor.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: "[U]nlawful or impractical" — the word "impractical", judged by Lender's own "reasonable opinion", is a soft trigger for a significant unilateral change, and "any change in market conditions" is unbounded.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 2.12(e) removes any matched-funding requirement, which weakens the factual premise for an impracticability claim; the two sit together awkwardly.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: One sentence, unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the LIBOR Rate and Reserve Percentage definitions.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A recital of consideration for joint and several liability; nothing operative to construe.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with the preamble's "jointly and severally" designation and Section 16.11.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Explicit co-debtor (not surety) characterisation; deliberately unambiguous.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Sections 2.13(d) and (i) and with the Obligations definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A short cross-default performance undertaking; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Consistent with Section 2.13(b) and Section 8.1.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: It describes the obligations as absolute "irrespective of the validity, regularity or enforceability of this Agreement", a self-undermining formulation, and it cites "Section 2.15", which does not exist.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: The intended reference is plainly Section 2.13, whose other subsections use the correct number; a mis-citation rather than a substantive clash.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: A long catalogue of waivers, each specifically identified and qualified by "to the extent permitted by applicable law"; comprehensive rather than uncertain.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It is qualified by "[e]xcept as otherwise expressly provided in this Agreement", which harmonises it with the notice requirements in Sections 8.2 and 9.1(k).

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Representations of informedness plus a forward covenant; determinate.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: It refers to "other guarantors, if any" although no Guaranty is required by Section 3.1 — a loose end shared with the Guarantor definition.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: The waiver is framed around "security for a guaranteed obligation" though these parties are co-debtors, not guarantors, and it cites "Section 580(d)" of the California Code of Civil Procedure.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: Section 13(a) makes New York law govern construction and enforcement, so a waiver drafted exclusively around California antideficiency statutes has an uncertain fit with the rest of the instrument.

judgments.reasoning_cat1: Sub-clause (B) refers to "Agent and Lenders" — parties that do not exist in this bilateral agreement — and the waiver assumes Real Property Collateral pledged by Borrowers.
judgments.reasoning_cat2: There is no Agent and only one Lender under the preamble, and Real Property is not an enumerated item of Borrower Collateral; the clause is carried over from a syndicated form and does not fit this instrument.
